title: Commit-message gate rules reach the commit scan
summary: Adds two structural commit-message rules — a subject that ends in a full stop, and a message with no subject — and makes the four structural rules CONTRIBUTING.md states (those two plus bare-reference and reference-without-label) run on both enforcement paths: the writing lint the commit-msg hook runs, and the commit scan used by pre-push and the pull request check. The scan previously ran only the configured scan rules, so a bad subject could pass a push; it now chains commit_gate_findings over each message. Rule docs gain a Coverage section, and docs/development.md gains a table of which rules each path checks.

lanes.subtitle: where a message is written
lanes.summary: The developer's commit and the git hooks that fire around it.

lanes.label: osf CLI
lanes.subtitle: commands and checkpoints
lanes.summary: The commands a hook or a CI job invokes, and the checkpoint that wraps them.

lanes.label: Writing lint
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/lints/writing
lanes.summary: The prose and commit-message detectors, their rule metadata, and the gate rule list.

nodes.label: Commit message
nodes.subtitle: subject + body
nodes.summary: The text a developer writes. Its structure — first non-blank, non-comment line, and the character it ends with — is what the new rules read.

nodes.label: commit-msg hook
nodes.subtitle: osf lint writing <msgfile>
nodes.summary: Thin hook that runs the writing lint over the message file. It already enforced the structural rules; the change adds the two subject rules to what it reports.

nodes.label: pre-push hook
nodes.subtitle: osf verify --stage pre-push
nodes.summary: Runs the pre-push checkpoint, which includes the commit scan over pushed messages.

nodes.label: osf lint writing
nodes.subtitle: --context commit
nodes.summary: The command the commit-msg hook calls. It resolves the writing lint in commit context and exits non-zero on an error-level finding.

nodes.label: osf check scan-commits
nodes.subtitle: pre-push checkpoint
nodes.summary: The checkpoint step that scans pushed commit messages; it calls the same scan_commits entry point as the scan command.

nodes.label: osf scan --commits
nodes.subtitle: range of hashes
nodes.summary: The command a pull request check runs over a commit range. Its exit code now reflects the gate rules, which the new integration test pins.

nodes.label: lint_writing
nodes.subtitle: fn lint_writing(text, known, cfg, Context::Commit, …)
nodes.summary: In commit context it now calls commit_subject_rules before the existing reference checks, so the hook path reports the two new rules.

nodes.label: commit_subject_rules
nodes.subtitle: fn commit_subject_rules(text, out)
nodes.summary: Finds the subject — the first line that is neither blank nor a `#` comment — and emits commit-subject-missing when there is none, or commit-subject-full-stop when it ends in one of four full stops.

nodes.label: commit_gate_findings
nodes.subtitle: fn commit_gate_findings(message, known)
nodes.summary: Runs the full writing lint in commit context with default config and no suppression, then keeps only the findings whose rule is in COMMIT_GATE_RULES. This is the bridge that lets the scan reuse the hook's detectors.

nodes.label: COMMIT_GATE_RULES
nodes.subtitle: 4 rule ids
nodes.summary: The list of rules a commit message must pass in a gate: the two subject rules plus bare-reference and reference-without-label. It is the single place that decides what the scan enforces.

nodes.label: RULE_META
nodes.subtitle: rule docs
nodes.summary: Rule documentation table. Gains entries for the two new rules and a Coverage section on the two reference rules describing where each is enforced and what it cannot decide.

nodes.label: scan_commits
nodes.subtitle: fn scan_commits(dir, range, rules)
nodes.summary: Loads known names once, then for each commit message runs the configured scan rules and extends the findings with commit_gate_findings. Findings stay unsuppressible because a message has no file to carry a marker.

nodes.label: Rules::scan_text
nodes.subtitle: configured scan rules
nodes.summary: The existing rule set applied to a message in commit context. It still runs first; the gate findings are appended to its output.

nodes.label: git access
nodes.subtitle: commit_hashes / commit_message
nodes.summary: Reads the commit range and each message body from the repository. Unchanged, but it is what makes the scan path independent of the hook.

nodes.label: load_known_names
nodes.subtitle: built-in names
nodes.summary: Loads the built-in known-name list the writing lint needs. Now called once per scan and once per check run instead of not at all on these paths.

nodes.label: commit_message_rules.rs
nodes.subtitle: both paths, pass and fail
nodes.summary: Integration tests that assert each gate rule fires on both the hook path and the scan path, that forge merge and dependency-bot messages pass, and that the scan and hook commands exit 0/1 accordingly.

nodes.label: docs/development.md
nodes.subtitle: coverage table
nodes.summary: Documents which CONTRIBUTING.md rules each path checks, which are deliberately unchecked, and the exemptions the checks read.

edges.label: commit context
edges.summary: The hook path gains the two subject rules here; this is the same detector the scan will reuse.

edges.label: per message
edges.summary: The scan path now runs the writing lint's gate rules over every message, closing the gap where a bad subject passed a push.

views.title: Commit-message enforcement paths
views.summary: Two entry points — the commit-msg hook and the commit scan — now converge on the same four structural rules.

views.title: Writing lint internals
views.summary: How the gate rule list, the subject detector and the rule metadata fit together inside the writing lint.
